unit.tutorContext: Module 3 teaches metabolic and adipose influences on facial architecture in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). dWAT: distinct adipocyte layer in the reticular dermis; reactive adipogenesis and cathelicidin against S. aureus and its age-related loss via TGF-β are mouse data (D); human dWAT is cone-shaped around follicles and human acne lesions contain cathelicidin-producing preadipocytes (D); its role in human skin ageing is unmeasured. Facial subcutaneous fat sits in discrete compartments (cadaver anatomy); in 186 identical-twin pairs higher BMI looked older before ~40 and younger after (C, observational). Glycation: AGEs accumulate in human skin collagen (~5-fold from 20 to 85 y, up to 2x in type 1 diabetes; skin collagen half-life ~15 y) — C; AGE cross-links and RAGE–NF-κB causing visible ageing: the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates B, the course grades D (lab/animal + associations); skin autofluorescence is a surrogate validated in non-pigmented skin; 'anti-glycation' products are tested on surrogates or appearance scores (guide grade C). Incretins: semaglutide (GLP-1 RA) and tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 RA). US status Sept 2026: Ozempic (T2D, 2017) and Wegovy (weight 06/2021; adolescents 12/2022; CV risk reduction 03/2024; MASH F2–F3 accelerated 08/2025); Mounjaro (T2D, 2022) and Zepbound (weight 11/2023; OSA 12/2024). Compounded, counterfeit and 'research' versions are not FDA-approved. STEP-1 −14.9% vs −2.4% (68 wk); SURMOUNT-1 −15.0 to −20.9% vs −3.1% (72 wk) — GRADE A for weight; median ~28% of weight lost is muscle-related (35 RCTs, B). Facial change ('Ozempic face'): retrospective imaging n=20, median 9% midface volume loss, mostly superficial, ~7%/10 kg (D); survey n=1,226, sagging/facial volume loss/hair loss rise with % weight lost (C); no RCT has measured the face; direct drug action on facial fat is a cell-study hypothesis. US labels list hair loss (~3–6% vs ~1% placebo, mostly women, linked to weight reduction) but not facial volume loss. Practice: counsel before treatment, photograph with consent, protect lean mass (protein, resistance training — no figures), refer restoration to a qualified aesthetic clinician; restoration advice is industry-linked expert consensus; decisions about stopping or changing the medicine belong to the prescriber and patient — never advise stopping, switching or dosing. Gut: inflammaging (IL-6/CRP predict frailty, death); metabolic endotoxaemia shown in mice and as a transient rise after a fatty meal in 12 men (D); restoring barrier function unproven for disease outside the gut; commercial zonulin ELISA detects other proteins. Probiotics for eczema: Cochrane 39 RCTs little/no patient-rated difference (B); children's meta-analysis small SCORAD gain (C). Rifaximin for rosacea with SIBO: small RCT (C). Tirzepatide + ixekizumab psoriasis: open-label Lilly phase 3b (C); liraglutide 20-person RCT negative (C); tirzepatide not approved for psoriasis in the US. Fibre: strong cardiometabolic evidence (guide grade A; review certainty moderate), no skin trials. Akkermansia pilot RCT metabolic only (C). 'Leaky gut' repair stack incl. BPC-157: guide grade D; BPC-157 not on the 503A bulks list (Sept 2026). Adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. UK (checked 25 Sep 2026): Ozempic licensed for T2D; Wegovy for weight management and CV risk reduction; Mounjaro for T2D and weight management under one brand (weight added 8 Nov 2023); UK SmPCs list hair loss (Wegovy 2.5%, Mounjaro 4.9% vs 1.0%); psoriasis not a UK tirzepatide indication; MHRA: retatrutide not authorised, illegal to sell (24 Jul 2026); largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines 28 May 2026; unlicensed 'specials' only for one patient's special clinical need, on the prescriber's responsibility (MHRA GN14). No CME credit is currently offered.

videoTranscript.en: Facial shape depends on fat as much as on collagen. In three lessons you will separate what is known about the skin's own fat, sugar damage to the dermis, weight-loss drugs and the gut from what is still mechanism, marketing or an open question. Most people picture skin fat as one layer under the dermis. There is a second, thinner layer inside the reticular dermis itself, called dermal white adipose tissue. In mice, this layer expands rapidly after a Staphylococcus aureus infection, and its new fat cells release cathelicidin, an antimicrobial peptide. Older mice lose much of that capacity, through TGF-beta signalling. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in small cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain preadipocytes around the follicle that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not yet been measured. So hold two things apart when you hear about skin fat. The defence story is strong in mice and emerging in people. The ageing story in people is still a proposal.

title.en: The skin keeps its own fat.

body.en: Beneath the dermis lies subcutaneous fat. Within the reticular dermis itself sits a thinner layer, dermal white adipose tissue. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not been measured.

body.en: Dermal white adipose tissue sits inside the reticular dermis, separate from the subcutaneous fat below. Fat as a whole is an endocrine organ that releases hormones such as leptin and adiponectin.
The layer expands after skin infection and its fat cells release cathelicidin. Older mice lose much of this capacity, through TGF-β signalling.
Human dermal fat clusters in cones around hair follicles, and acne lesions contain preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. Its part in skin ageing is unmeasured.

title.en: Fat that holds the face up.

body.en: Cadaver dissection shows that the face's subcutaneous fat sits in separate compartments, and facial ageing is partly how each compartment changes. Weight shows the same thing from the outside. In a study of 186 pairs of identical twins, the twin with the higher body-mass index looked older before about age 40 and younger after it.

blocks.sourceNote: Rohrich & Pessa 2007 · Guyuron 2009

label.en: pairs of identical twins compared for facial ageing

detail.en: Guyuron et al., 2009 — a four-point higher BMI tracked with an older look before about 40 and a younger look after it

means.en: From midlife on, facial fat goes with a younger-looking face. That fits the anatomy: the face ages partly as its fat compartments change. GRADE C, observational.

doesNot.en: It is an observational comparison of photographs. It does not show that gaining weight rejuvenates, or that fat loss on a drug changes the skin itself.

body.en: Glycation is a slow, non-enzymatic reaction. Reducing sugars attach to protein amino groups, rearrange into Amadori products and end as advanced glycation end products, or AGEs. On long-lived dermal collagen, AGEs form cross-links that stiffen the matrix. Through their receptor, RAGE, AGEs switch on inflammatory signalling in laboratory studies. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects B; the course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.

body.en: Reducing sugars bind protein amino groups, form a reversible Schiff base, then a more stable Amadori product, and finally irreversible AGEs.
Structural: AGEs cross-link collagen and elastin and stiffen the dermis. Signalling: AGEs bind RAGE, which drives NF-κB and inflammatory cytokines in cell and animal studies.
The Hormonaly endocrinology guide rates both B. The course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.

audioScript.en: Glycation is chemistry before it is biology. Reducing sugars attach to the amino groups of proteins, rearrange into more stable products, and end as advanced glycation end products, known as AGEs. Dermal collagen lasts for years, so it collects AGEs, and they form cross-links that make the matrix stiffer. AGEs also bind a receptor called RAGE, which in laboratory studies switches on inflammatory signalling and enzymes that break down matrix. Keep the registers apart here. The chemistry, and the build-up of AGEs in human skin, are well documented. The idea that AGEs cause the wrinkles and laxity you see in clinic rests on laboratory and animal work plus human associations. The Aesthetic and Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects grade B. This course grades the causal link D, and the next moment shows why.

title.en: Fifteen years on the same collagen.

body.en: Human skin collagen turns over slowly; tissue analysis puts its half-life at about 15 years. In skin biopsies, glycoxidation products in collagen rose about five-fold between ages 20 and 85, and were up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes. Skin autofluorescence, a non-invasive reading, correlates moderately with those biopsy measures and was validated in non-pigmented skin.

body.en: GLP-1 and GIP are incretins, hormones the gut releases after a meal that amplify glucose-dependent insulin release; GLP-1 also slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 is broken down within minutes. Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, and tirzepatide activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. In the US, as of September 2026, both are FDA-approved drugs for defined indications, set out in the next moment.

body.en: GLP-1 from intestinal L-cells and GIP from K-cells amplify insulin release when glucose is high. GLP-1 also slows the stomach and reduces appetite.
Native GLP-1 is cleared within minutes by the enzyme DPP-4. The drug molecules are modified to last far longer in the blood.
In the US, semaglutide is sold as Ozempic and Wegovy, tirzepatide as Mounjaro and Zepbound, and the brand tells you the approved use.

audioScript.en: After a meal, the gut releases two hormones called incretins, GLP-1 and GIP. Both amplify insulin release when glucose is high, and GLP-1 also slows the stomach and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 lasts only minutes in the blood before an enzyme breaks it down, so the drug molecules are engineered to last far longer. Semaglutide activates the GLP-1 receptor. Tirzepatide activates both the GIP and the GLP-1 receptors. Those are the mechanisms. The regulatory facts sit in a separate register. In the United States, as of September 2026, both molecules are FDA-approved drugs, sold under one brand name for type 2 diabetes and another for chronic weight management, with further indications for the heart, the liver and sleep apnoea. The face appears nowhere on those labels, and that is where this lesson begins.

text.en: In the UK both are licensed by the MHRA, and tirzepatide's diabetes and weight-management uses share one brand, Mounjaro.

In the EU, semaglutide is a centrally authorised prescription medicine, as Ozempic and Rybelsus for diabetes and Wegovy for weight management (EMA and HMA, June 2024), and tirzepatide is authorised as Mounjaro (EU-wide, 15 September 2022) for diabetes and adult weight management, prescription-only. A search of the Union Register and EMA's medicines data on 25 September 2026 found no EU product named Zepbound.

In Brazil, ANVISA has registered semaglutide as Ozempic (since 6 August 2018) and Wegovy (since 2 January 2023), with synthetic semaglutide pens registered from 26 May 2026, and tirzepatide as Mounjaro (since 25 September 2023); a search of its register on 25 September 2026 found no product named Zepbound. Since 23 June 2025, GLP-1 receptor agonist medicines may only be sold with retention of the prescription (RDC 973/2025 and IN 360/2025).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has been the federal authority regulating medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and its register lists semaglutide as Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy and tirzepatide as Mounjaro; every entry checked is a Prescription Only Medicine. A search of the EDE register on 25 September 2026 found no product named Zepbound.

text.en: In the UK (MHRA, September 2026), Ozempic is licensed for diabetes and Mounjaro for diabetes and weight. Wegovy is licensed for weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction; MHRA added weight management to Mounjaro in November 2023. MHRA says retatrutide is not authorised in the UK and anyone selling it does so illegally (24 July 2026), and in May 2026 it made its largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines.

In the EU, semaglutide is authorised as Ozempic for diabetes (since 8 February 2018) and Wegovy for weight management (since 6 January 2022), and tirzepatide as Mounjaro for diabetes and adult weight management (since 15 September 2022), all prescription-only. In June 2024 EMA and HMA's shortage steering group said GLP-1 receptor agonists are not approved for, and should not be used for, cosmetic weight loss, and on 3 September 2025 EMA and HMA warned of a sharp rise in illegal medicines sold online and on social media as semaglutide, liraglutide or tirzepatide, which are unauthorised and may not contain the stated substance.

In Portugal, Wegovy and Mounjaro are authorised through the EU centralised procedure and are prescription-only, and on 4 July 2024 INFARMED stated that Ozempic, Trulicity and Victoza must not be prescribed to patients who are not diabetic (Circular 045/CD/100.20.200). In September 2025 INFARMED relayed the EMA and HMA warning of a sharp increase in the illegal marketing of medicines presented as GLP-1 receptor agonists, and stated that in Portugal medicines can only be bought on the internet from the websites of pharmacies and licensed non-prescription medicine outlets (LVMNSRM).

In Brazil, as of September 2026, Ozempic is indicated for adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, Wegovy is indicated for weight management in adults, Mounjaro is indicated for chronic weight management in adults, and the approved synthetic semaglutide copies are indicated for adult patients with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus. Nota Técnica 200/2025 (August 2025) permits compounding of chemically synthesised APIs provided registered medicines with the same molecule already exist in Brazil, and ANVISA inspections from January to April 2026 led to the closure of 8 of the 26 establishments assessed and the seizure of more than 1.3 million units of irregular injectable medicines.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) announced on 1 June 2026 that it had approved oral Wegovy (semaglutide) for long-term weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related conditions, and a Ministry of Health and Prevention alert (Circular 9217/2024, October 2024) described genuine Mounjaro as registered for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 bars compounding pharmacies from compounding essential copies of products that hold an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient. On 20 July 2026 the EDE warned that 1,659 packs of Mounjaro and Ozempic missing from a warehouse are outside the legitimate supply chain and told the public to buy these medicines only from licensed pharmacies.

audioScript.en: Ageing brings a slow rise in background inflammation, called inflammaging. It is low-grade and sterile, and in older adults higher IL-6 and C-reactive protein predict frailty, disability and death. One proposed source is the gut. In mice, a high-fat diet raises bacterial lipopolysaccharide in the blood, and infusing that endotoxin reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance. In twelve healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. That is the mechanism usually called metabolic endotoxaemia, or leaky gut. The human evidence stops short of the skin. Measuring gut permeability is difficult, and a leading review concludes that it is still unproven whether restoring the barrier improves disease outside the gut. Hold that line as you look at what patients are sold.

audioScript.en: Patients often link their skin to their gut. Start where the evidence is. Diet quality, treatment of metabolic disease and the established treatment for the skin condition itself all come first. Be careful with tests. A widely used commercial zonulin assay was shown to detect proteins other than zonulin, so a result cannot tell you whether a gut is leaky. Be careful with products too. Probiotics are strain-specific, and their effects on eczema are small at best. The Hormonaly guide gives the popular gut-repair stack of glutamine, zinc carnosine and BPC-157 a grade of D. As of September 2026, in the United States, BPC-157 remains off the 503A bulks list after the July advisory-committee review. Investigational peptides come last, if at all. Whatever your role, name the evidence type before you name the product.

prescriber.en: Treat the skin disease on its own evidence and metabolic disease directly. A zonulin result should not guide care. In the US, BPC-157 has no 503A bulks-list standing as of September 2026, so compounding it for gut repair is not an option.

clinical-staff.en: If a patient brings a gut-repair kit or a zonulin result, record the products and the result and bring them to the prescriber. Do not interpret the test or advise on the products.

text.en: In the United Kingdom, an unlicensed peptide reaches a patient only through narrow routes, such as a special ordered for one patient's clinical need, which module seven sets out.

In the EU, Directive 2001/83/EC allows a medicine on the market only with a national or EU-wide marketing authorisation (Article 6(1)), while medicines prepared in a pharmacy for an individual patient on prescription (magistral formulas) fall outside the directive and need no marketing authorisation under it (Article 3). Each member state may also, under its own law, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a bona fide unsolicited order from an authorised health professional, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Article 5(1)).

In Portugal, no medicine containing BPC-157 is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register (25 September 2026). A medicine is defined as any substance or combination of substances presented as having properties for treating or preventing disease or that may be used or administered to restore, correct, or modify physiological functions through pharmacological, immunological, or metabolic action (Estatuto do Medicamento, Article 3). INFARMED does not authorise importing medicines for personal use, and a compounded medicine may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese Pharmacopoeia, the European Pharmacopoeia, pharmacopoeias of other States Parties to the European Pharmacopoeia Convention, or compendial scientific documentation (Decreto-Lei 95/2004, Article 6).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have undergone efficacy and safety assessments before it can be compounded, and that some injectable peptides are not regularised in any category (food, medicine, cosmetic or food supplement) and are illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use. ANVISA also stated in July 2026 that an investigational medicine is used exclusively in authorised clinical research.

In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, in force since 2 January 2025, bars importing, selling or using any medical product without a marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), and lets a physician prescribe a medicine never submitted for approval only when necessary, when no equivalent alternative is available and with the patient's approval. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits using any research-use peptide on humans, or for treatment, outside a study or clinical trial approved by the competent authority (29 July 2026). prompt.en: A patient shows you this fictional sales page for a 'gut–skin reset' kit. Which sentences does the evidence not support?

text.en: Background inflammation rises slowly with age; researchers call it inflammaging.

why.en: Supported. Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age.

text.en: In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty and death.

why.en: Supported, as a prediction: in older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty, disability and death.

text.en: Studies show that a high-fat diet raises gut bacterial toxin in the blood, and that the toxin causes weight gain and insulin resistance.

why.en: Shown in mice. There, a high-fat diet raised bacterial lipopolysaccharide in the blood, and infusing it reproduced weight gain and insulin resistance; the page leaves out the species.

text.en: In a small study of healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised endotoxin in the blood within four hours.

why.en: Supported: in 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. A short rise in a small study; the human evidence stops short of the skin.

text.en: That leak is what drives acne, eczema and rosacea.

why.en: Not shown. Whether a leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been shown.

text.en: Seal the barrier with this kit and your skin clears from the inside out.

why.en: Unproven. Restoring barrier function has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut.

text.en: A fibre-rich diet has strong evidence for heart and metabolic health.

why.en: Supported, for the heart and metabolism: the guide grades it A, and the review behind it rates certainty moderate. No trial has measured skin.

hint.en: Ask where each sentence was shown: in mice, in a small human study, or nowhere yet.

done.en: The supported sentences stop short of the skin; the leaps rest on a mouse result told as a human one and on skin benefits no study has shown.

prompt.en: Closing Module 3: which statement keeps the four registers apart?

text.en: Semaglutide ages the face by acting on facial fat, so the label should carry a facial warning.

why.en: That blends an untested hypothesis with a regulatory conclusion. The labels list hair loss; a direct action on facial fat is untested in people.

text.en: Facial volume loss on incretins: fat loss deflates facial compartments (mechanism); small observational studies tie it to the amount of weight lost (human evidence); US labels list hair loss but not facial change (regulatory status); whether the drugs act directly on facial fat is untested (open question).

why.en: Correct. Four separate answers, each with its own source.

text.en: Weight loss on these drugs is GRADE A, so their facial effects are GRADE A too.

why.en: A grade belongs to an outcome. The pivotal trials never measured the face.

feedback.en: One grade per outcome, one register per sentence.

prompt.en: A colleague says tirzepatide is 'GRADE A', so its effect on the face must be well established. What is wrong with that reasoning?

text.en: Nothing: a drug's grade applies to all of its effects.

why.en: Grades attach to a specific outcome in a specific population. The pivotal trials measured weight and never the face.

text.en: Grades attach to outcomes: weight loss is A from large randomized trials, while facial change rests on small observational studies.

why.en: Correct. One grade per outcome.

text.en: Tirzepatide has no GRADE A evidence for anything.

why.en: It does, for weight management and type 2 diabetes, from large randomized trials such as SURMOUNT-1.

rationale.en: An evidence grade belongs to a statement, not to a molecule. SURMOUNT-1 supports an A for weight loss; facial change rests on a 20-patient imaging study and a patient survey (C to D), and no randomized trial has measured the face.

prompt.en: Which statement about the gut–skin link is best supported by the evidence?

text.en: Probiotic capsules reliably clear eczema by repairing the gut barrier.

why.en: Pooled trials show little or no difference in patient-rated eczema symptoms.

text.en: Metabolic endotoxaemia is shown in mice and small human studies, but restoring the gut barrier has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut.

why.en: Correct. Mechanism in mice and short-term human physiology; no proof that barrier repair helps the skin.

text.en: A zonulin blood test identifies patients whose skin disease comes from a leaky gut.

why.en: A widely used zonulin assay detects proteins other than zonulin.

rationale.en: High-fat feeding raises circulating endotoxin in mice and briefly in healthy men; a leading review finds it unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut, and Cochrane found little or no patient-rated benefit from probiotics in eczema.

keys: should i stop ozempic because of my face

answer.en: 'Ozempic face' describes facial hollowing and laxity during weight loss on incretin drugs. Mechanism: losing fat deflates the superficial facial fat compartments and unmasks laxity already present. Human evidence is observational and small: one retrospective imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost (D), and a survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost (C). No randomized trial has measured the face. Regulatory status (US, September 2026): semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) are FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, chronic weight management and further heart, liver and sleep-apnoea indications. Their labels list hair loss (about 3–6% on drug against about 1% on placebo, mostly in women, linked to weight reduction) but not facial volume loss. In the UK (September 2026), Ozempic is licensed for type 2 diabetes, Wegovy for weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction, and Mounjaro for both type 2 diabetes and weight management; UK product information also lists hair loss, and MHRA says retatrutide is not authorised in the UK. Open question: whether the drugs act directly on facial fat, beyond weight loss, rests on cell studies. In practice: raise facial and hair changes before treatment, record concerns with consented photographs, refer restoration requests to a qualified aesthetic clinician, and take any question about stopping or changing the medicine to the prescriber. The course gives no dosing advice.

Mechanism: bacterial lipopolysaccharide crossing a leaky gut barrier ('metabolic endotoxaemia') drives inflammation and insulin resistance in mice, and a single high-fat meal briefly raised plasma endotoxin in a study of 12 healthy men (D). Human evidence for skin: an independent Cochrane review of 39 trials found probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms (B); a 2024 meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported small score improvements (C); one small randomized trial found rosacea improved after small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth was treated (C). A leading review concludes it is unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut, and a widely used commercial zonulin assay detects proteins other than zonulin. A fibre-rich diet has strong evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes and has not been tested on skin outcomes. The Hormonaly guide grades the 'leaky gut' repair stack (L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, BPC-157) D; in the US, BPC-157 is not on the 503A bulks list as of September 2026. In the UK, an unlicensed medicine can be supplied as a 'special' only for an individual patient's special clinical need that no licensed product meets, on the prescriber's responsibility. Start with diet, metabolic health and the skin diagnosis; investigational peptides come last, if at all, and any injected or research peptide needs a prescriber.
